pharm: GnRH agonist; continuous administration suppresses gonadotropin secretion and gonadal steroidogenesis after an initial surge
quick: Depot 7.5 mg SC monthly, 22.5 mg every 3 months, 30 mg every 4 months, or 45 mg every 6 months
Not applicable; administered by subcutaneous injection
Contraindicated in pregnancy; can cause fetal harm in non-prostate indications
Not indicated in women requiring lactation; not for use during breastfeeding
Serum testosterone and PSA, blood glucose, bone density, cardiovascular status, QT in at-risk patients
summary: Leuprolide acetate is a GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone) agonist used as androgen deprivation therapy for advanced prostate cancer and, in other formulations, for endometriosis, uterine fibroids, and central precocious puberty. Continuous dosing initially stimulates then profoundly suppresses pituitary gonadotropins, lowering testosterone or estrogen to castrate levels. An early testosterone surge can transiently worsen disease (tumor flare).
indications: Treatment of advanced prostate cancer (depot subcutaneous formulation)
Other formulations are indicated for endometriosis, uterine leiomyomata (fibroids), and central precocious puberty (per product-specific labeling)

dosage.t: Administered by a healthcare provider; vary injection site in soft subcutaneous tissue

admin: Must be administered by a healthcare provider as a subcutaneous injection
Vary the injection site periodically; use an area with sufficient loose subcutaneous tissue (e.g., upper or mid-abdomen)
Avoid areas with brawny or fibrous subcutaneous tissue
Reconstitute and prepare strictly per product-specific instructions immediately before use
Consider concomitant anti-androgen during the first weeks in patients at risk of tumor flare
moa: Leuprolide acetate is a GnRH agonist. Given continuously at therapeutic doses it acts as an inhibitor of gonadotropin secretion. After an initial stimulation (surge of LH, FSH, and testosterone or estrogen), chronic administration results in down-regulation of pituitary GnRH receptors and suppression of testicular and ovarian steroidogenesis, producing medical castration. This effect is reversible after discontinuation.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to GnRH, GnRH agonist analogs, or any component of the product (anaphylactic reactions reported)
Pregnancy (for non-prostate indications) and undiagnosed abnormal vaginal bleeding
relative: Pre-existing cardiovascular disease (increased MI, stroke, sudden cardiac death risk)
monitor: Bone mineral density with long-term use
ECG/QT in patients with risk factors

preg: Leuprolide is contraindicated in pregnancy when used for non-prostate (female) indications; it can cause fetal harm and may increase the risk of pregnancy loss based on its mechanism. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective non-hormonal contraception. The prostate cancer indication is in men.
lact: Leuprolide is not indicated for use in women who are breastfeeding, and use during lactation is not recommended. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, do not breastfeed during treatment.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment for renal impairment has been established. Use the standard depot regimen with clinical monitoring.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment for hepatic impairment has been established. Use the standard depot regimen with clinical monitoring.

major: QT-prolonging drugs (additive risk of QT prolongation with androgen deprivation therapy)
moderate: Antihyperglycemic agents (leuprolide may raise glucose and require dose adjustment)
Drugs affecting cardiovascular risk in patients on androgen deprivation
minor: Tests of pituitary-gonadal function are altered during and after therapy
interactions.food: Not applicable; administered by subcutaneous injection
interactions.diagnostics: Suppresses the pituitary-gonadal axis; diagnostic tests of pituitary gonadotropic and gonadal function during therapy and after discontinuation may be misleading

serious: Tumor flare (worsening symptoms from initial testosterone surge)
Myocardial infarction, stroke, and sudden cardiac death
rare: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
emergency: Spinal cord compression or ureteral obstruction from tumor flare (urinary retention, weakness, paralysis) - seek emergency care
Severe skin reaction with blistering or mucosal involvement - stop and seek emergency care
Acute chest pain, stroke symptoms, or seizure - emergency care

monitoring: Serum testosterone and PSA to confirm and maintain castrate suppression
Symptoms of tumor flare during the first weeks of therapy in patients with metastatic disease
Cardiovascular risk and ECG/QT in susceptible patients
Bone mineral density during long-term androgen deprivation therapy
counsel: This medicine is given as an injection by your healthcare provider on a fixed schedule; keep your appointments
Symptoms such as bone pain or urinary difficulty may briefly worsen when treatment starts (tumor flare); report severe symptoms
Hot flashes, reduced sexual interest, and tiredness are common
Report any rash with blistering, chest pain, sudden weakness, or seizures immediately
Long-term treatment can weaken bones and raise blood sugar; follow advice on diet, exercise, calcium and vitamin D
pk: Initial gonadotropin/testosterone surge within days; castrate suppression usually within 2-4 weeks
Peak serum leuprolide shortly after injection, then sustained release from depot
Terminal elimination half-life approximately 3 hours (parent drug)
Depot provides continuous suppression for 1, 3, 4, or 6 months depending on formulation
Store per product-specific labeling; typically at controlled room temperature, protect from freezing
pearls: Watch for tumor flare from the initial testosterone surge; an anti-androgen may be co-administered in high-risk metastatic prostate cancer
Warnings include hyperglycemia/diabetes, increased cardiovascular events (MI, stroke, sudden death), QT prolongation, convulsions, and severe cutaneous adverse reactions
Long-term androgen deprivation reduces bone density; consider bone-protective measures
Confirm castrate testosterone and falling PSA to assess response
missed: Leuprolide depot is given on a fixed schedule by a healthcare provider. If a scheduled injection is missed, contact the clinic to receive it as soon as possible; do not self-administer. Delays may allow testosterone to rise and reduce treatment effect.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. In animals, very high doses produced effects attributable to the pharmacologic action. In humans, overdose is managed with supportive care and monitoring. Contact Poison Control (1-800-222-1222).
